newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Weather great for key Brazil soybean states - coops.
newsitem.headline: Weather great for key Brazil soybean states - coops.

text.p: The weather remains optimal for the soybean crop in Brazil's top two growing states, Parana and Rio Grande do Sul, cooperatives said.
Rains last week left good soil moisture, and now sunshine is helping the crop's development, producers said.
"Everything is going normally. We had good rains a week ago and now temperatures are perfect -- seasonal to hot," said an official of Coamo cooperative in Parana.

In Cascavel, Ernani Camapanati of Coopavel cooperative said conditions were marvellous. "It has not rained in the past few days but there is good soil humidity. Temperatures are also good, a little above normal."
In Rio Grande do Sul, practically all of the crop was in the vegetative stage, said Valdir Bisotto of state cooperatives' federation.
"If conditions keep like this, we should see a 26 million tonne (Brazilian) crop," said Jaime Tonon, superintendent of Santa Barbara cooperative.

However, it was unlikely the crop would be much higher than this because farmers had insufficient resources to buy fertilizers and other necessary inputs which should have been applied at the time of planting, he said.
